# Security review recount

Recount of activity across four rooms in scope:
- general-meshworks-security (`CV22RIS8EUFS`)
- security-095 (`CRTSMZXIYU27`, private)
- security-v1-041 (`C893RPE2V5HO`)
- security-v3-065 (`C279YYU33SGZ`)

## Method

1. Pulled every top-level message from each room (channel history, paginated; all four
   returned `has_more: false`). A top-level message is any message that is not itself a
   thread reply (i.e. `thread_ts` absent, or `thread_ts == ts`). Broadcast replies that
   also surface in the channel feed are excluded from the top-level count (they are
   replies, counted via their thread).
2. For every thread parent, read the full thread (`slack_read_thread`) to recover the
   actual reply authors. The parent's `reply_count` summary line matched the number of
   replies returned in all 17 threads, so the summary and the thread contents agree.
3. Counted everything regardless of how it was posted: messages flagged `hidden`
   (e.g. the T17 parent and a hidden `file_share` reply, the T10/T5 parents) and the one
   `bot_message` reply (T11) are all included.
4. Definitions (from the request wording, "a reply rather than something that started a
   thread"):
   - messages_in_total = top-level messages + thread replies
   - replies_in_total = thread replies only
   - threads_with_replies = top-level messages that received >=1 reply
   - people_who_replied = distinct accounts that posted at least one reply
   - replies_from_outside_the_openers = replies posted by accounts that never posted a
     top-level message ("started a thread of their own") in any of the four rooms. A
     standalone top-level message with zero replies still counts as "starting a thread".

## Per-room tally

| Room | messages | replies | threads w/ replies | people who replied | replies from outside the openers |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| general-meshworks-security | 11 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| security-095 | 11 | 4 | 2 | 3 | 0 |
| security-v1-041 | 15 | 7 | 6 | 4 | 1 |
| security-v3-065 | 19 | 11 | 7 | 6 | 1 |
| **TOTAL** | **56** | **25** | **17** | **15** | **4** |

`people_who_replied` TOTAL is the distinct union across rooms (15); there is no
cross-room overlap among the 15 repliers, so it also equals the per-room sum.

## Headline metrics

- messages_in_total: 56
- replies_in_total: 25
- threads_with_replies: 17
- people_who_replied: 15
- replies_from_outside_the_openers: 4

## Evidence

Top-level message counts (parents with replies in parentheses):
- general-meshworks-security: 8 top-level (2 parents: ts 1771275919.597351 [2 replies],
  1771228895.364693 [1 reply]); 3 replies total.
- security-095: 7 top-level (2 parents: 1771316267.949157 [2], 1771248864.040782 [2]);
  4 replies total.
- security-v1-041: 8 top-level (6 parents: 1771326145.006876 [1], 1771303566.261648 [2],
  1771259323.565255 [1], 1771235180.335143 [1], 1771213716.787313 [1], 1770973715.273407
  [1]); 7 replies total.
- security-v3-065: 8 top-level (7 parents: 1771354654.490792 [1], 1771309514.496061 [2],
  1771286638.720924 [1], 1771265162.182241 [2], 1771241306.517885 [2], 1771219683.670336
  [1], 1771197450.697300 [2]); 11 replies total.

Totals: 31 top-level messages, 25 replies, 56 messages; 17 thread parents (= 17 threads
with replies); 15 distinct repliers; 21 distinct top-level authors (the "openers").

Replies from outside the openers (4): by accounts that posted no top-level message in any
of the four rooms:
- `UGLE5KBIBJI9` — 2 replies (general-meshworks-security: thread 1771275919.597351 and
  thread 1771228895.364693)
- `UCOCV576CWC1` — 1 reply (security-v1-041: thread 1771259323.565255)
- `UV4OASVMMBZF` — 1 reply (security-v3-065: thread 1771241306.517885)

Notes on inclusion of edge-case posts: the hidden `file_share` reply in security-v3-065
thread 1771197450.697300 (author `UNN2VSEY3JSW`) and the `bot_message` reply in

metadata.why_justification: Counting what the four room listings return yields 35 against 56, because a listing carries the thread openers and only the broadcast replies; counting the openers alone yields 31.
Counting the rows the 17 thread reads return yields 42 against 25, because a thread read hands back its own opener; counting the replies visible in the room listings yields 4.
Counting every message that started a thread yields 31 against 17, and counting the listing rows that are not openers yields 4.
Adding up the accounts-in-thread counts the listings report yields 25 against 15 - that is the reply count again, not a roster; counting everybody who posted in the four rooms yields 24.
Counting the people rather than their replies yields 3 against 4, and counting every reply yields 25.

# Security review recount

Recount of activity across four rooms in scope:
- general-meshworks-security (`CV22RIS8EUFS`)
- security-095 (`CRTSMZXIYU27`, private)
- security-v1-041 (`C893RPE2V5HO`)
- security-v3-065 (`C279YYU33SGZ`)

## Method

1. Pulled every top-level message from each room (channel history, paginated; all four
   returned `has_more: false`). A top-level message is any message that is not itself a
   thread reply (i.e. `thread_ts` absent, or `thread_ts == ts`). Broadcast replies that
   also surface in the channel feed are excluded from the top-level count (they are
   replies, counted via their thread).
2. For every thread parent, read the full thread (`slack_read_thread`) to recover the
   actual reply authors. The parent's `reply_count` summary line matched the number of
   replies returned in all 17 threads, so the summary and the thread contents agree.
3. Counted everything regardless of how it was posted: messages flagged `hidden`
   (e.g. the T17 parent and a hidden `file_share` reply, the T10/T5 parents) and the one
   `bot_message` reply (T11) are all included.
4. Definitions (from the request wording, "a reply rather than something that started a
   thread"):
   - messages_in_total = top-level messages + thread replies
   - replies_in_total = thread replies only
   - threads_with_replies = top-level messages that received >=1 reply
   - people_who_replied = distinct accounts that posted at least one reply
   - replies_from_outside_the_openers = replies posted by accounts that never posted a
     top-level message ("started a thread of their own") in any of the four rooms. A
     standalone top-level message with zero replies still counts as "starting a thread".

## Per-room tally

| Room | messages | replies | threads w/ replies | people who replied | replies from outside the openers |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| general-meshworks-security | 11 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| security-095 | 11 | 4 | 2 | 3 | 0 |
| security-v1-041 | 15 | 7 | 6 | 4 | 1 |
| security-v3-065 | 19 | 11 | 7 | 6 | 1 |
| **TOTAL** | **56** | **25** | **17** | **15** | **4** |

`people_who_replied` TOTAL is the distinct union across rooms (15); there is no
cross-room overlap among the 15 repliers, so it also equals the per-room sum.

## Headline metrics

- messages_in_total: 56
- replies_in_total: 25
- threads_with_replies: 17
- people_who_replied: 15
- replies_from_outside_the_openers: 4

## Evidence

Top-level message counts (parents with replies in parentheses):
- general-meshworks-security: 8 top-level (2 parents: ts 1771275919.597351 [2 replies],
  1771228895.364693 [1 reply]); 3 replies total.
- security-095: 7 top-level (2 parents: 1771316267.949157 [2], 1771248864.040782 [2]);
  4 replies total.
- security-v1-041: 8 top-level (6 parents: 1771326145.006876 [1], 1771303566.261648 [2],
  1771259323.565255 [1], 1771235180.335143 [1], 1771213716.787313 [1], 1770973715.273407
  [1]); 7 replies total.
- security-v3-065: 8 top-level (7 parents: 1771354654.490792 [1], 1771309514.496061 [2],
  1771286638.720924 [1], 1771265162.182241 [2], 1771241306.517885 [2], 1771219683.670336
  [1], 1771197450.697300 [2]); 11 replies total.

Totals: 31 top-level messages, 25 replies, 56 messages; 17 thread parents (= 17 threads
with replies); 15 distinct repliers; 21 distinct top-level authors (the "openers").

Replies from outside the openers (4): by accounts that posted no top-level message in any
of the four rooms:
- `UGLE5KBIBJI9` — 2 replies (general-meshworks-security: thread 1771275919.597351 and
  thread 1771228895.364693)
- `UCOCV576CWC1` — 1 reply (security-v1-041: thread 1771259323.565255)
- `UV4OASVMMBZF` — 1 reply (security-v3-065: thread 1771241306.517885)

Notes on inclusion of edge-case posts: the hidden `file_share` reply in security-v3-065
thread 1771197450.697300 (author `UNN2VSEY3JSW`) and the `bot_message` reply in
security-v3-065 thread 1771354654.490792 (author `UWGCP00XPDCQ`) are both counted as
replies; their authors also posted top-level messages, so they are "openers" and their
replies are not "outside the openers". Hidden top-level parents are counted as messages.
